lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
Date of birth: 3 Mar 1997 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Cut the card-dispute form's abandonment rate from 37% to 22% in a four-week A/B test by splitting it into three short steps with saved progress.
- Brought the design system to WCAG 2.1 AA by setting body-text contrast to at least 3:1 against every background.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Presented quarterly findings to the head of product and two design teams; three of the top five recommended fixes shipped in the next release cycle.
- Trained 12 product managers to run their own unmoderated tests with a shared script template, which doubled the number of tests run each quarter.
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Raised the patient app's Net Promoter Score from 6.1 to 8.4, calculated as the average 0-10 recommendation rating across 2,000 monthly survey responses.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; the findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Writes the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Cut median route-finding time from 90 to 60 seconds, a 50% improvement, by adding audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
- Raised task success by 20% across 12 participants, from 65% to 85%, with audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Redesigned a free clinic's online booking flow, cutting the steps to book from 9 to 4; phone bookings fell by a quarter in the next two months.
- Recruited 10 clinic patients and ran two rounds of hallway testing, fixing the six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA), Tableau
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interveiws, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: Check that the portfolio link works and leads directly to relevant UX research work.
Remove the date of birth and nationality for most U.S. job applications.
If space becomes tight, consider removing the education location and dates.
items.because: They are less valuable than your experience.

items.says: Clarify your research role versus the form design and implementation.
Include the A/B test size if available.
items.because: It helps readers assess a four-week result.

items.says: A 3:1 contrast ratio does not meet WCAG 2.1 AA for ordinary body text.
Changing text contrast alone does not establish that the entire design system meets WCAG 2.1 AA.
items.because: The claim should state only the criterion and scope verified.

items.says: Fix the opening grammar to match the completed actions in the bullet.
Clarify how the synthesis led to the 23% reduction in repeat support calls.
items.because: The current wording skips the intervention.

items.says: Specify what made the three shipped fixes your recommendations.
Clarify whether testing doubled across the 12 PMs, their teams, or the organization.
items.because: That defines the scale of the outcome.

items.says: Identify your research contribution to the shipped design without implying it caused the entire sign-up increase.
items.because: A post-launch change alone does not prove that the research or design caused all of the increase.

items.says: The average of 0–10 recommendation ratings is not Net Promoter Score.
Clarify whether the 2,000 responses apply to each comparison period.
Clarify whether the missed-appointment rates cover comparable periods and populations.
Specify how the interviews informed the two-way reminder.
Change the present-tense verb to past tense.
Clarify whether the setup-time reduction applies to all studies or a measured subset.
Clarify the period and population behind the 30% reduction in support calls.
Identify what the waiting-room testing revealed or changed, if possible.
Keep “Present” only if you are still actively working on the map.
Clarify what participants actually used in testing.
items.because: A Figma design, a screen-reader-accessible prototype, and an implemented map support different claims.

items.says: The change from 90 to 60 seconds is a 33% reduction in time, not a 50% improvement.
Specify whether the before-and-after medians came from comparable tasks.
The change from 65% to 85% is a 20-percentage-point increase, not a 20% relative increase.
Explain what the percentages are based on with 12 participants.
items.because: The precision needs to make sense, perhaps through multiple tasks.

items.says: Consolidate the repeated mention of audio landmarks and colors across the two results bullets.
Define the comparison behind the drop in phone bookings.
Do not assume fewer phone bookings reflect successful online booking without supporting evidence.
items.because: Fewer calls may reflect successful online booking, but the résumé does not establish that.

items.says: Clarify how the two testing rounds led to the six fixes, including whether any were tested again.
items.because: That would make the research process more convincing.

items.says: Clarify whether the later teams used the handbook specifically when adding Spanish-language booking.
items.because: They may have merely used it at some point.

items.says: Correct the typo “interveiws.”
Account for the interval since the last listed employment ended in June 2025.
items.because: Relevant work since then could be added; otherwise, be ready to explain the interval in interviews.
